Package com.bilt.pos.session

Class ReversalSession

java.lang.Object
com.bilt.pos.session.ReversalSession
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
public final class ReversalSession extends Object implements AutoCloseable
A referenced reversal of a prior sale — void or refund from a fresh session, in a later process, long after the CheckoutSession that took the payment is gone.

The builder carries the POI references the POS persisted from the original sale's CheckoutResult: the card and stored value (gift card) legs, the committed rebate and redemption movements, the loyalty award, and the member. voidTransaction() reverses every referenced movement; refund()/refund(BigDecimal) return money against the card leg and reverse the award. Reversing the payment this session's own checkout just took needs no references — CheckoutSession does that itself.

For an item-based refund, ring the returned items into the session's refund cart (basket()) — every line is a credit line, so each mutation refreshes the customer display with negative amounts — and execute with refundBasket(), which refunds the cart total against the card leg with the returned items attached. Which items and quantities may be returned is the register's call; the cart itself is free-form.

Like a checkout, the session is bracketed on the terminal: the builder's start() announces it (Nexo Admin session start signal) and end() tells the terminal to discard its session-scoped data; try-with-resources sends the end signal even on exception paths. All operations are lazy — nothing is sent until execute(), get(), or getOrNull() is invoked — and run blocking on the calling thread.


 try (ReversalSession session = ReversalSession.builder()
         .client(client)
         .saleId("POS-LANE-3")
         .poiId("VictaLane-275839164")
         .currency("USD")
         .poiTransactionId(stored.cardTxnId)
         .poiTransactionTimestamp(stored.cardTs)
         .redemptionPoiTransactionId(stored.redemptionTxnId)
         .awardPoiTransactionId(stored.awardTxnId)
         .memberId(stored.memberId)
         .start()
         .get()) {
     session.voidTransaction().execute();
 }

Sessions are intended for use from a single register thread; abort() is the one method safe to call from another thread.

    • basket

      public SessionBasket basket()
      The session's refund cart: the items being returned, rung in like a checkout basket. Every line is a credit line — totals are negative and, with autoDisplay enabled (the default), each mutation refreshes the customer display with the itemised returns. Mutations are allowed until a void or end() seals the session; refundBasket() consumes the cart. The cart is free-form — whether an item may be returned, and in what quantity, is the register's decision.

    • voidTransaction

      public ReversalFlow<VoidResult> voidTransaction()
      Reverses every referenced movement of the original sale, in order: the card and stored value legs (Nexo ReversalRequest), then the committed redemption, rebate, and award (their LoyaltyRequest refund types). Only the movements a reference was supplied for are reversed; a sale with no money leg (rewards covered everything) is voided by its loyalty references alone.

      When a step fails, the flow's onError handler decides between retry, skip, and abort — see ReversalFlow for the default policy. A retried void resumes at the first movement still standing — reversed movements are never re-credited, and the retry's VoidResult describes only the movements that call sent. Not allowed once a refund has returned money from this session. The session moves to SessionState.VOIDED on success.

    • refund

      public ReversalFlow<RefundResult> refund()
      Full linked refund of the referenced card leg. Also reverses the loyalty award when awardPoiTransactionId was supplied — best-effort by default (override via ReversalFlow.onError(java.util.function.BiFunction<com.bilt.pos.session.ReversalStep, com.bilt.pos.session.SessionError, com.bilt.pos.session.ReversalDecision>)).

      Linked refunds reference a single transaction — the card leg. Use voidTransaction() to reverse every movement of the sale, including its rebate and redemption. Repeated partial refunds are allowed (the acquirer enforces the cumulative limit), but once a refund has returned money the sale can no longer be voided from this session. A tender skipped by an onError decision leaves the sale voidable, and an award the flow reversed is remembered — neither a void nor a retried refund re-credits it. Once a void has partially reversed the sale's money legs, refunds are refused until the void is finished.

    • refund

    • refundBasket

      public ReversalFlow<RefundResult> refundBasket()
      Item-based linked refund: refunds the refund cart's total against the referenced card leg, with the returned items attached to the refund's PaymentRequest. Also reverses the loyalty award when awardPoiTransactionId was supplied — best-effort by default, like refund(), and subject to the same guards.

      The cart is consumed (cleared, with a display refresh under autoDisplay) the moment the tender refund moves money — even when a later award step aborts the flow, so a retry can never re-send the same returns. While no money has moved — the refund failed, or the tender was skipped by an onError decision — the cart stays intact for a retry. Ring the next return into basket() for a further partial refund — the acquirer enforces the cumulative limit.

    • abort

      public void abort()
      Best-effort abort of the in-flight request. Money-moving operations always deliver their outcome even when the abort raced them: the movement may have completed on the terminal, and the register must know. Safe to call from any thread; with nothing in flight this is a no-op.

    • end

      public SessionResult<Void> end()
      Ends the session: tells the terminal to discard the session-scoped data it accumulated and moves the session to SessionState.ENDED, from which no operation is allowed. Not allowed while a void is in flight (state VOIDING). If the end signal fails, the session keeps its current state so the call can be retried.
